newsitem.title: USA: American, pilots extend strike deadline.
newsitem.headline: American, pilots extend strike deadline.

text.p: American Airlines said Tuesday that it and the Allied Pilots Association have agreed to a new timetable that extends the potential for a strike beyond an April 28 deadline.
The agreement delays any strike until at least 30 days after a rejection by either side, the company said.

The pact gives both sides a 30-day cooling off period before a strike coul begin in the event a tentative labour pact between both parties is rejected, said Al Comeaux, a spokesman for American Airlines.
The labour pact must first be approved by the board of the Allied Pilots Association and then by the union membership. The board is scheduled to meet April 3.
Comeaux said the agreement also ensures Congress is in session on the day that a strike would begin.
Last week, the pilots' union and the nation's second-largest carrier reached a labour agreement, but the accord was tentative and required approval by the union's board and by member pilots.

The main issues in the dispute, which caused a brief strike last month before Clinton stepped in, had been wages and whether APA pilots would fly new commuter jets American is buying for its regional carrier, American Eagle.
American is a unit of Fort Worth, Texas-based AMR Corp.
